transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s my eating. What scares me is that once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I’ve kind of stepped aside and I can’t make myself stop. I’ll be telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away,” but I just… don’t. 

And it’s silly, because I can keep track of other things fine—like I can remember where I put the mail or what day the trash goes out—but with food in that moment, it’s like I’m not in charge of my own hands.
After these episodes of eating that you can’t seem to stop, do you ever try to compensate in any way, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Um… I don’t really know how to answer that exactly. I mean, I feel awful after, and sometimes I’ll tell myself I should “make up for it,” but I’m not sure what counts. Like, I’ll get distracted and start thinking about how I need to clean the fridge or throw away the snack wrappers before anyone sees them, and then I’m just embarrassed.

So… I don’t think I have a clear answer about doing those specific things.
Do you ever try to make up for these eating episodes by exercising more than you normally would?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t… I mean, I’m not someone who suddenly goes and runs for hours or anything like that. Sometimes I’ll think, “I should take a walk,” but then I get caught up in something else, like putting things away or checking the pantry, and it sort of becomes this whole other thing in my head.

So I don’t think I have a clear pattern with exercise, if that’s what you mean.
After these eating episodes, do you ever fast, severely restrict your food intake, or do anything else extreme to try to control your weight or the calories you consumed?

I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had times where I think, “Well, maybe I just won’t eat much tomorrow,” but then tomorrow comes and I’m thinking about appointments or whether I paid the electric bill, and it doesn’t become some planned thing exactly.

I wouldn’t say I have a clear answer about fasting or doing anything extreme. I guess I’m not sure what you’d count as severe, honestly.
Can you tell me if these episodes where you feel like you can’t stop eating happen even when you’re not hungry, and if they continue until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah… a lot of the time it’s not really hunger. Like, I’ll already have had supper, and my stomach isn’t asking for anything, but I still end up going back to the pantry or opening the fridge. Sometimes I’m just standing there looking, and then I start picking at things, and it turns into… more than I meant.

And then, yes, I guess it can go until I feel really uncomfortable. Like I know I should stop before that, but I keep going back anyway.
During these times when you're eating and feel like you can't stop, would you describe it as feeling completely out of control, like you're not making the choices anymore?

Yes… I think that’s the part that scares me. Once I start, especially if I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I’ve sort of stepped aside from myself, if that makes sense.

I’ll be telling myself the whole time, “Janet, put it away, just close the bag, put it back,” but my hands are still reaching for more. It doesn’t feel like I’m calmly choosing it. It feels like I can’t get myself to stop, even though I know I should.
Do these episodes where you feel out of control with eating cause you a lot of distress or worry, even when you're not in the middle of one?

Yes… I do worry about it afterward. Not right that second sometimes, because I’m sort of just sitting there, and then I look around and realize what I ate, and I feel awful.

I’ll think, you know, that was food I meant to save or share, and now it’s gone because I couldn’t just leave it alone. And then I get mad at myself, like, I’m 48 years old, I should not be acting like this in my own kitchen. I’ll sit there ashamed and tell myself, “That’s it, Janet, you’re not doing this again.” But then… well, I guess that’s why I’m here.
Do you usually end up eating this way when you're by yourself, and does the idea of someone finding out about these episodes make you feel especially upset?

I… I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I notice it more when I’m by myself, maybe just because there’s nobody interrupting me or asking what I’m doing. But I haven’t really kept track of whether that’s always the case.

As for someone finding out… I don’t know. I guess I wouldn’t want people talking about it, but I haven’t really thought about that part clearly. It’s more like I try not to think about it at all afterward, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal during these episodes where you feel out of control?

Yes… I think so. I don’t really notice it at first, but then I’ll realize I’m eating so fast I’m barely even tasting it. Like if I made a casserole or muffins or something, I’ll just be standing there at the counter taking bite after bite.

It’s strange because I’m not actually late for anything. I don’t have anywhere I need to be right then, but I eat like I’m in a hurry. And then I’ll look down and think, why was I doing that so fast? Like I didn’t even enjoy it properly.
Do you usually eat this way when you're alone because you're worried someone might see you or because you'd be embarrassed if they did?

I don’t know if it’s because I’m worried someone might see me, exactly. I mean, I suppose I’d feel embarrassed if someone walked in, but I haven’t really sat there thinking, “I need to be alone so no one catches me.”

It’s more like… I just notice it happens when things are quiet and I’m in the kitchen, and then my mind wanders. Sometimes I’m putting things away or cleaning up, and one thing turns into another. I’m not sure I’ve connected it to being seen, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you eat this way more often when you're alone because you're worried someone might see you or because you'd feel ashamed if they did?

I know you’re asking that again, and I wish I had a cleaner answer. I really don’t know if it’s because I’m afraid someone will see me. I haven’t noticed myself thinking it through that way.

I mean, I’d probably be uncomfortable if someone did walk in, sure, but that’s different from saying that’s why I’m alone when it happens. Sometimes being alone just means the house is quiet and I’m sort of on autopilot. Then later I try to avoid thinking about it too much, so it’s hard to say what was driving it.

During these times when you feel out of control with eating, would you say that you're eating a very large amount of food—like a whole box of cookies or an entire meal—within a short period of time, maybe even just a couple of hours?

Yes… yes, I think that’s fair to say. It’s not always like a neat example, like “I ate exactly a whole box of this,” but there are afternoons where it’s a lot in a short time.

Like after I’ve been at the food bank, or if I’ve been baking banana bread or cookies for something at the senior center—because I do try to help with those things, and then there’s always extras or ends of things—I’ll come home and start with maybe a plate of leftovers. And then it’s a slice of banana bread, then another one, then chips, some cheese, whatever cookies are in the tin… and at the time it sort of feels like I’m just picking at things.

But afterward, when I look back at it, I think, that was way more than I would ever put on a plate and serve someone as a meal. So yes, it can definitely be a very large amount.
